$comment: Synced from Figma file 0tJgH96ncHm4HFAkRGrAVm, page 'monadic — v0'. Names are the contract. Generates the Tailwind theme and CSS custom properties. Nothing else in the codebase may contain a raw design value. status: 'from-figma' means the value came from a Figma variable or a measured frame; 'derived' means it was read off frame geometry because Figma has no variable for it, and wants confirmation.

canvas.$comment: Warm cream, not grey. The old #f4f3f1 was warm in name and neutral on screen; both reference systems ground on an actual cream (#f0eee6, #ffffeb) and it is most of why they read warm.

base.$comment: Cards. Off-white rather than pure white — #ffffff on a cream canvas reads as a hole punched in the page.

sunken.$comment: Wells, hovers, muted chips. Warm sand.

hover.$comment: Between base and sunken, so a hovered control darkens without reading as pressed.

secondary.$comment: Darkened from #6e6e68. Measured on the new cream ground the old ramp put tertiary at 2.5:1 — under AA for the small text it carries, and the previous palette had the same problem on its own ground. The whole ramp moved down a step instead of squeezing tertiary into secondary: primary 15.2, secondary 7.3, tertiary 4.8, all on canvas.

tertiary.$comment: Was secondary. 4.8:1 on canvas and 5.3:1 on base, so captions and meta lines clear AA on both grounds rather than only looking like they do.

inverse.$comment: Matches surface/base, so inverse text is the same off-white as a card.

focus.$comment: Unchanged. Ink, at full contrast on every surface here.

accent.$comment: Ink remains the workhorse for primary controls; coral is the one warm accent, reserved for the action that leaves the app. See DESIGN.md section 1.

default.$comment: Ink. Still what a primary control is made of.

signal.$comment: The only non-neutral color in the system. Positive and live signals only.

status.$comment: Pipeline states. Never the only signal — always paired with a label (DESIGN.md section 9).

badge.$comment: StatusBadge. Colour groups stages; the label and glyph carry the distinction, never colour alone (DESIGN.md section 9).

neutral-bg.$comment: Withdrawn — a stage that ended without a decision.

teal-bg.$comment: The three live interview stages share one hue; the glyph and label separate them.

coral.$comment: The second non-neutral, and the deliberate break from the old one-accent rule. Wispr Flow's flare is #ff6c4c and Anthropic's terracotta is #d97757; this sits between them. Text on coral is INK, not white: white measures 3.5:1 here and ink measures 4.8:1, and darkening the coral far enough for white to pass turns it brown. Dark text on a warm fill is what Anthropic does with the same colour.

default.$comment: Apply, and nothing else on a card. One coral thing per row.

hover.$comment: Lighter, not darker — ink sits on this, so a darker hover would reduce the contrast the label depends on. Ink measures 5.6:1 here against 4.8:1 at rest.

space.$comment: Figma defines no spacing variables, so these are measured off the v0 frames. tight=tag/meta gap, snug=card internal gap, comfortable=card padding-x, default=card padding-y and board gutter, loose=feed grid gutter.

logo-card.$comment: 44px — the feed card tile. Smaller than logo/68px because the card was rebuilt to one row: the tile now sits beside three text rows rather than beside a column that also carried a footer, and at 68px it outweighed the title it was introducing. The detail page header keeps 68px, where the company is the subject rather than a label.

hair.$comment: 3px — the dot separating company from posted date.

row.$comment: 7px — gap between the card's meta, title and tag rows.

body.$comment: 16px — gap between preview tile and detail column; card padding-bottom.

dot-sm.$comment: 5px — status dot on the pipeline card.

line.$comment: 4px — the two-line stack inside the dock's resume card.

cozy.$comment: 12px — dock resume-card gap and review-banner inset.

entry-x.$comment: 13px — horizontal inset of a dock list entry.

entry-y.$comment: 11px — vertical inset of a dock list entry.

panel-x.$comment: 28px — horizontal inset of the job detail header card, frame 50:348.

logo-sm.$comment: 34px — the company tile inside a rail panel.

sans.$comment: Figtree. Replaces Inter: rounder terminals and a taller x-height read warmer at 13px, which is where this interface lives.

numeric.$comment: Same face. Figtree ships tabular figures, so comp columns still align.

display.$comment: EB Garamond, italic only. Page titles and empty states — places addressing a person. Never a row, a tag or a figure.

meta.$comment: 10px — the date line on a dock entry.

figure.$comment: Compensation in the card footer. 15px, between body and lead.

monogram.$comment: 24px — fallback initial in the CompanyPreview tile.

tracking.$comment: Negative tracking applies at 17px and above only (DESIGN.md section 3).

wide.$comment: 0.72px at 9px — the dock's uppercase section labels.

shadow.$comment: Cards separate from the warm canvas by value, not by shadow. Only the raised nav pill lifts.

panel.$comment: 640px — the filter popover. Wide enough for three columns of options without becoming a page-width band.
